paragraphs: Swamiji used a tiny image from Indian tradition to explain something vast. Picture a doll made of salt that decides to find out how deep the ocean is. It wades in and sinks down to measure it. But the deeper it goes, the more it dissolves, until it melts away completely and becomes one with the sea it set out to measure.

Ordinary individual souls, Swamiji said, are just like that salt doll. Try to reach the bottom of the Infinite and you don't come back with a measurement; you discover you were made of the same stuff all along. The whole matter, he said, comes down to one thing: knowing that you are the eternal Brahman.
learn: Some truths can't be studied from the outside like a lab sample; you only grasp them by being changed by them. The idea that your real self is part of something infinite can make everyday worries feel much smaller.
